title: Understanding the Median Salary Melbourne and How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert hourly pay to annual salary using a 38-hour week and 52-week year. Explore the median salary Melbourne, tax, super, and fortnightly pay estimates.
salarySummary: For a 38-hour week and 52-week year, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52. The National Minimum Wage is $26.44/hour, giving $52,254.80 annually before tax and super.

faqs.q: How do I convert my hourly rate to an annual salary?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, assume 38 hours per week. For example, $30/hour × 38 × 52 = $59,280 gross per year. If you work fewer weeks (e.g., casual or part-year), adjust the 52-week figure may overstate your actual annual earnings.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates and casual loading?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage (from 1 July 2026) is $26.44/hour for full-time employees. Award rates are higher for specific industries and are set by the Fair Work Commission. Casual employees receive a 25% loading on top of their base rate (e.g., $33.05/hour for minimum wage). Superannuation is paid on top of ordinary earnings at 12%.

faqs.q: How is tax and super calculated on my annual pay?
faqs.a: For 2026–27, tax uses the resident scale: nil up to $18,200; 15% from $18,001 to $45,000; 30% from $45,001 to $120,000; 37% from $120,001 to $180,000; 45% above $180,000. Medicare levy is 2% (using 2025–26 reduction thresholds). Super is 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, up to the $270,830 maximum contribution base. These are estimates only.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Calculate Annual Pay from an Hourly Rate

If you know your hourly rate, you can estimate your annual gross salary using a simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks**. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week for a full year, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For most full-time employees in Australia, the standard week is 38 hours, as defined by the Fair Work Ombudsman.

For example, if you earn $30 per hour and work 38 hours each week, your annual gross pay is:

$30 × 38 × 52 = $59,280

This figure is before tax, Medicare, and superannuation. It also does not include casual loading, which is an extra 25% on top of the base rate for casual employees (see [casual loading](/topics/casual-loading) for details).

### The National Minimum Wage and Award Rates

From 1 July 2026, the National Minimum Wage is $26.44 per hour, or $1,004.90 per week for 38 hours. Casual employees receive $33.05 per hour including the 25% loading. However, many workers are covered by award rates that are higher than the minimum. Award rates vary by industry and classification, and you can check your specific award using [pay guides](/blog).

If you are comparing your pay to the **median salary Melbourne**, note that the Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) publishes average weekly earnings, not median figures. The ABS Average Weekly Earnings (May 2026) for full-time adult ordinary time is $2,083.70 per week, which is an average, not a median. The median salary in Melbourne is often discussed in job advertisements and industry reports, but no single official figure is published for all occupations. For a more tailored comparison, refer to [job pay](/topics/job-pay) resources.

### Fortnightly and Weekly Pay

Many employers pay fortnightly. To find your fortnightly gross pay, simply multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the $30/hour example:

- Weekly: $30 × 38 = $1,140
- Fortnightly: $1,140 × 2 = $2,280

This helps when budgeting or comparing salary offers that are quoted per fortnight.

### Tax and Superannuation

Your annual gross pay is used to estimate tax and super. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- $0 – $18,200: nil
- $18,201 – $45,000: 15% on excess over $18,200
- $45,001 – $135,000: $4,020 plus 30% on excess over $45,000
- $135,001 – $190,000: $31,020 plus 37% on excess over $135,000
- $190,001 and above: $51,370 plus 45% on excess over $190,000

Medicare levy is generally 2% of taxable income. The 2025–26 single reduction thresholds are used here because the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of calculation. For a more accurate estimate of your take-home pay, use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

Superannuation guarantee is 12% of your ordinary earnings, paid on top of your salary by your employer. It is not deducted from your hourly rate. The maximum contribution base for super is $270,830 per year. For example, on a $59,280 salary, your employer would contribute $7,113.60 in super (12% of $59,280). Learn more about [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging).

### Important Considerations

The formula annual gross = hourly × hours per week × 52 is a starting point. It assumes you work every week of the year with no unpaid leave. If you are casual or work part-time, your actual annual earnings may differ. Also, award rates may include penalty rates for weekends or overtime, which are not captured here.

For a quick calculation, you can use the [timesheet](/), where you enter your base hourly rate and optionally add casual loading. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading; use the checkbox instead.

### Using Reference Tables

For a broader view of typical pay, the [reference tables](/data) provide average weekly earnings by industry and state. Remember, these are averages, not medians. The **median salary Melbourne** is a common benchmark but varies by occupation and experience. Always check your specific award or enterprise agreement for your exact entitlements.

### Summary

- Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52 (if full-time)
- National Minimum Wage: $26.44/hour; casual: $33.05/hour
- Super is 12% on top, up to $270,830
- Tax and Medicare are deducted from gross pay
- Fortnightly pay = weekly pay × 2

Use the [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for current rates, and the [hourly conversion](/topics/hourly-conversion) guide for more examples.
